sources.title: Argentina's Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, Argentine Republic
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate trends mainly cover 1960–2010; the Adaptation Communication also summarizes regional vulnerabilities and end-century RCP8.5 projections.
sources.methodology: Second NDC Adaptation Communication summarizes climate observations, projections and regional vulnerabilities.
sources.limitations: Regional impacts draw on earlier assessments; dates, scenarios and local population data vary.

sources.title: Tools for understanding the dynamics of the 7 March 2025 flood in Bahía Blanca
sources.organization: Instituto Nacional del Agua, Hydraulic Laboratory, Argentina
sources.temporal_coverage: Technical analysis of the 7 March 2025 flood, using event observations and a preliminary hydrodynamic model.
sources.methodology: INA combines public-video flood marks, hydrological data and a 2D hydrodynamic model for the four urban watersheds.
sources.limitations: First version; sparse public observations and simplified channel/terrain inputs limit precision.

sources.title: Resolution 532/2025: Supplement for Reconstruction rules, updated text
sources.organization: Ministry of National Security, Argentine Republic
sources.temporal_coverage: Rules for the one-time housing recovery subsidy after the 7 March 2025 Bahía Blanca flood, including July 2025 amendments.
sources.methodology: Official legal text defines eligibility, payment zones, verification and monitoring procedures for the SUR subsidy.
sources.limitations: The regulation establishes program rules, not the number of eligible applicants, payments made or resulting recovery.

sources.title: Storm impacts and resources sent to Bahía Blanca
sources.temporal_coverage: Provincial emergency update at 18:00 on 7 March 2025.
sources.methodology: Provincial government emergency communication lists reported rainfall and resources deployed during the response.
sources.limitations: This is an event-day government update, not an independent evaluation or a record of final outcomes.

sources.title: National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2025–2029
sources.organization: National System for Integral Risk Management and Civil Protection, Argentina
sources.temporal_coverage: National disaster-risk priorities and targets for 2025–2029.
sources.methodology: Government summary describes the plan's objectives, participatory formulation and expected 2029 results.
sources.limitations: The webpage reports planned objectives and expected results; it does not establish implementation or achievement.

sources.title: Water situation and runoff forecast for Mendoza, 2026–2027 season
sources.organization: Department General of Irrigation, Government of Mendoza Province
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed 2025–2026 runoff and provincial flow forecasts for the 2026–2027 water season.
sources.methodology: Provincial water authority reports seasonal river-flow forecasts based on year-round monitoring and nine automated stations.
sources.limitations: The webpage summarizes seasonal volumes and does not state uncertainty ranges or climate-model scenarios.

claims.locator: Second NDC, Adaptation Communication, PDF p. 46, observed hydrological changes
claims.paraphrase: It reports 1960–2010 rainfall change expanded permanent water bodies in east/central Buenos Aires and southern Santa Fe/Corrientes, including Mar Chiquita and La Picasa.
geographies: eastern and central Buenos Aires Province
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
claims.limitations: Trend is historical; source notes high rainfall variability.

claims.locator: Second NDC, Adaptation Communication, PDF p. 46, end-century precipitation projection
claims.paraphrase: For end-century RCP8.5, it projects 10–20% less rainfall in western Patagonia and the Mendoza Andes, with similar increases in central/eastern Argentina.
affected_groups: communities and producers in the named regions
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
claims.limitations: Regional projection, not a local impact forecast.

claims.locator: Second NDC, Adaptation Communication, PDF p. 48, regional vulnerability table
claims.paraphrase: NDC identifies low-income Indigenous populations as exposed due to ecosystem dependence, fragile livelihoods, limited voice and territorial displacement.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
claims.limitations: It does not attribute specific displacement to climate change.

claims.locator: Second NDC, Adaptation Communication, PDF p. 47, regional vulnerability table
claims.paraphrase: NDC expects climate impacts to increase internal migration in search of better livelihoods.
claims.scenario: No specific emissions scenario or migration horizon is given.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
claims.limitations: No routes, scale or conflict outcome is estimated.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The NDC expects climate impacts to increase internal migration for livelihoods (p. 47).

claims.locator: INA technical report, printed pp. 5 and 21–22, reported impacts and maximum flood marks
claims.paraphrase: INA's April report records 16 reported deaths and 1,000+ evacuees; estimated depths reached 2.0 m in Barrio Napostá and 0.8 m in Ingeniero White.
affected_groups: residents of Barrio Napostá and Ingeniero White
claims.limitations: Marks use few public videos, concentrated in media-covered areas.

claims.locator: INA technical report, printed pp. 25–28, Canal Maldonado velocity estimates
claims.paraphrase: Video analysis at Canal Maldonado/Agustín Álvarez estimated surface flows of 3.5–4.5 m/s; an impact-based estimate approached 5 m/s.
affected_groups: residents and people using the canal crossing
claims.limitations: Image obstructions and simplifying assumptions limit precision.

claims.locator: INA technical report, printed pp. 5–8 and 45–46, model coverage and shared tools
claims.paraphrase: INA shared a preliminary 2D model of four Bahía Blanca watersheds, calibrated with public-video flood marks.
claims.limitations: INA identifies missing drainage and topographic inputs.

claims.locator: INA technical report, printed pp. 7–8 and 45–46, watershed definition and model limitations
claims.paraphrase: Study domain covers Bahía Blanca, Ingeniero White and General Cerri across the Napostá and Sauce Chico basins; smaller drains were omitted.

claims.locator: Resolution 532/2025, Annex sections 3–5, eligibility and payment zones
claims.paraphrase: The one-time SUR subsidy is limited to one payment per affected home for its regular resident; it excludes applicants in homes above ground level and differentiates high- and medium-impact zones.
affected_groups: adult regular residents of affected homes
claims.limitations: These are published eligibility and payment rules; the regulation does not show who was actually excluded or paid.

claims.locator: Resolution 532/2025, Annex sections 14–15, vulnerable housing and supplementary application
claims.paraphrase: The rules define vulnerable flood-affected homes for a subsidy component as those without an electricity meter and allow a 72-hour follow-up to correct incomplete or unverified applications.
affected_groups: residents of flood-damaged homes without electricity meters
applicants with incomplete or unverified documentation
claims.limitations: The text establishes the administrative design, not the number of households reached or whether the follow-up window was used.

claims.locator: Resolution 532/2025, Annex sections 2, 9–13, transparency and payment monitoring
claims.paraphrase: The subsidy rules require public process information, cross-checking with utility and public-agency records, applicant status tracking, and ministry monitoring of payments.
claims.limitations: These are mandated procedures; the regulation does not evaluate transparency, processing times or payment completion.

claims.locator: Buenos Aires Province emergency update, 7 March 2025, emergency resources
claims.paraphrase: The Province reported an interministerial emergency committee and deployed rescue personnel, boats, emergency shelters, food, water, ambulances and municipal coordination to Bahía Blanca.
claims.limitations: The statement records deployments announced on event day, not the quantity delivered or effectiveness of assistance.

claims.locator: Buenos Aires Province emergency update, 7 March 2025, hospital response
claims.paraphrase: The Province reported evacuating Hospital Penna and transferring patients to Bahía Blanca's municipal hospital and private clinics; mobile intensive care and ambulances were sent.
institutions: Buenos Aires Province Ministry of Health
claims.limitations: The official event-day statement does not report patient numbers, clinical outcomes or later service restoration.

claims.locator: National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction webpage, formulation process and priorities
claims.paraphrase: Argentina's 2025–2029 plan sets priorities for risk understanding, SINAGIR coordination, coordinated provincial and municipal preparedness, and resilient recovery.
institutions: National System for Integral Risk Management and Civil Protection
claims.limitations: These are plan priorities and expected results through 2029, not verified implementation outcomes.

claims.locator: National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction webpage, participatory formulation
claims.paraphrase: The plan's technical formulation used ten SINAGIR commissions involving government, scientific agencies, universities, civil society and business representatives.
affected_groups: government, technical, academic, civil-society and business stakeholders
claims.limitations: The webpage identifies participating categories but does not describe representation or influence in particular decisions.

claims.locator: Mendoza water forecast webpage, runoff volumes for the 2026–2027 season
claims.paraphrase: Mendoza's DGI forecasts above-average 2026–2027 runoff for the Mendoza (129%), Tunuyán (117%), Diamante (112%) and Grande (111%) rivers, and near-average Atuel and Malargüe flows.
claims.scenario: Provincial seasonal runoff forecast for 2026–2027 relative to mean flow; not an emissions scenario.
claims.limitations: This is a seasonal forecast, not realized runoff; the page does not provide uncertainty intervals.

claims.locator: Mendoza water forecast webpage, forecast production and monitoring network
claims.paraphrase: DGI says its year-round flow forecasting informs reservoir management for irrigation, energy and consumption and uses nine automated monitoring stations across Mendoza.
claims.limitations: The page describes the forecasting system but does not independently evaluate coverage or its effect on water allocation.

search_audit.query: Argentina named provincial climate vulnerability rainfall drought flood heat Indigenous livelihoods NDC
search_audit.outcome: Read the Second NDC and INA 2025 technical report; found regional water and livelihood risks and named flood depths and infrastructure in Bahía Blanca, Napostá and Ingeniero White.

search_audit.query: Argentina climate impacts internal migration Indigenous forced displacement livelihoods climate security conflict
search_audit.outcome: The Second NDC expects climate-related internal migration and identifies pre-existing displacement and livelihood vulnerabilities among low-income Indigenous peoples; it does not attribute violence or conflict to these pathways.

search_audit.query: Argentina conflict insecurity violence disrupting disaster response climate adaptation provincial evidence
search_audit.outcome: No Argentina-specific primary evidence was found that conflict or insecurity disrupted climate adaptation, water forecasting or emergency response; this remains an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Argentina provincial flood recovery subsidy disaster risk governance seasonal water forecast Mendoza adaptation capacity
search_audit.outcome: Opened the federal disaster-risk plan, Bahia Blanca subsidy rules and provincial response statement, and Mendoza's 2026–2027 runoff forecast; planned systems are distinguished from reported deployments and outcomes.

gaps: No existing ARG country baseline was present in the assigned worktree.
The Second NDC's migration statement is a broad expected effect without source/destination, scale or forced-migration estimates; it does not identify conflict as an outcome.
The NDC identifies Indigenous territorial displacement as a vulnerability but does not establish that climate change caused specific displacement events.
The 2022 National Adaptation and Mitigation Plan PDF exceeded the available extraction limit; no claims rely on its search excerpt.
INA's Bahía Blanca model is an initial version with incomplete drainage and topographic inputs; its local observations are sparse and media-skewed.
The SUR rules and federal disaster-risk priorities document design, not completed benefit payments or plan implementation.
No Argentina-specific primary evidence was found that conflict or insecurity has disrupted climate adaptation or emergency services; this is not evidence of absence.
